title: Top Use Cases for Agentic and Interactive Demos
summary: While websites remain the most popular, interactive demos are expanding across the entire GTM funnel, from sales outreach to user training.
body_markdown:
Marketers know B2B buyers want to try before they buy. It’s why nearly[one in every five B2B SaaS websites](https://www.navattic.com/report/state-of-the-interactive-product-demo-2026) has an interactive demo CTA.


But interactive demos aren’t just a way to capture the attention of people visiting your site for the first time. They can also help you stand out in paid campaigns, post-event follow-ups, blogs, and docs.


That said, a demo you’d put on your homepage isn’t necessarily the one you’d send after a webinar or hand to a champion making your case to their team.


Which is why more GTM teams are turning to[demo automation](https://www.navattic.com/blog/what-is-demo-automation) , a quicker way to spin up and personalize demos at scale – and one that helps deals[close 19 days faster](https://www.navattic.com/report/state-of-demo-automation-2026) .


Some are even experimenting with[agentic demos](https://www.navattic.com/blog/what-are-agentic-demos) ,[interactive product experiences](https://www.navattic.com/blog/agentic-vs-interactive-demos) powered by AI, to bridge the gap between a completely self-serve tour and a full-blown demo with an SE.


Below, we’ll cover the top use cases for interactive demos, automated demos, and agentic demos at each stage of your customer journey.


Top of funnel


At the top of the funnel, demos help generate awareness and educate potential customers.


Traditionally, brands rely on blog content, ebooks, and webinars to do the heavy lifting. Interactive demos perfectly complement these assets, allowing readers to try out your product as they learn about it.


### Use case 1: Website call-to-actions


Adding interactive demos to your website offers two main benefits:


1. They give your prospects a chance to do their own research without talking to sales.
2. They increase your website’s efficiency, since engaged visitors are more likely to convert.


The[team at LogicMonitor](https://www.navattic.com/blog/how-logicmonitor-turned-an-AI-product-tour-into-lead-generation) saw this firsthand.


After their team built a product tour to help visitors understand Edwin, their new agentic platform, **more than half of engaged visitors converted into leads** .


And those leads show up to sales calls far more informed and interested.


Per Margo Poda at LogicMonitor, *“When somebody explores our Navattic demo, it’s a much stronger signal. Our sales team knows this person already understands the product, so reps can tailor follow-up to what they explored and get to deeper questions sooner.”*


Today, the Edwin tour is LogicMonitor’s top lead-generating asset (for 18 months and counting).


Want some helpful tips for adding interactive demos to your website?


**Read more here:**[Incorporating Interactive Demos into a Website Redesign](https://www.navattic.com/blog/interactive-demos-website-redesign)


### Use case 2: Paid campaigns & social media


Instead of directing traffic to static landing pages, use interactive demos.


Encouraging users to explore your product is much less of a lift than asking them to book a demo or sign up for (and actually use) a free trial. Plus, prospects immediately see product value, which is why interactive demos tend to improve paid ad click-through rates.


[Notion](https://www.navattic.com/blog/how-to-plan-build-and-share-demos-for-demand-gen) is a good example.


Describing the product in words is very difficult. As Tiffany Hsia at Notion puts it:


*“We have a unique challenge in that we are a very horizontal product. Some people refer to it as their second brain because we connect all knowledge, workflows, projects and AI into a flexible tool.”*


They decided the best way to explain Notion was to show it. So they worked with[DemoDash](https://www.navattic.com/demo-consultants?consultant=demo-dash) to develop and execute their interactive demo strategy.


One aspect of that strategy was running gated demos on LinkedIn, targeted to specific audiences, such as engineering and product teams.


So far, their demos have influenced more than $5 million in pipeline.


But PPC isn’t the only way to promote your tours. Several Navattic customers use Reddit Ads to catch the eye of new buyers.


[Cvent](https://www.reddit.com/user/cvent/comments/1hxoqn4/explore_cvent_with_our_interactive_tour_today/) , for instance, has encouraged Redditors to take a tour of their product, including compelling stats and social proof to push users to act.


Clicking on the ad takes users straight to Cvent’s interactive demo.


Want to learn how to add demos to paid ads?


**Here are 3 ways to do it with 3 real examples:**[Ad Best Practices for Product Demos](https://www.navattic.com/blog/product-demos-ads)


### Use case 3: Event & webinar follow-ups


Your prospects probably aren’t going to re-listen to the webinars you recorded or remember everything you talked about at a conference.


Instead of sending slides, recordings, or boring one-pagers, send them an interactive demo. To maximize your click-through rate, also include:


- Bullet points to remind prospects how your product meets their needs.
- What users should expect to see in your demo.
- Other helpful collateral tailored to their needs.
- A clear call to action.


With[Launchpad](https://www.navattic.com/product/launchpad) , you can search for relevant pre-built demos, make some tweaks for the event, and send custom demos as follow-ups. That way, you’re not starting from scratch.


Take[Map My Customers](https://www.navattic.com/blog/how-map-my-customers-solved-event-demo-chaos) . As they scaled their event marketing, it was becoming harder and harder to maintain demo consistency.


Meghan Rodino on their marketing team decided to adapt the product tours they had specifically for event use.


*“They included all of our new features, different prompts for event audiences, and were available on mobile, so our reps could show various features from their phones.”*


Then, post-event, the team sent relevant follow-up demos to keep the leads warm. Overall, they saw a 28% increase in total converted accounts.


Even more impressive, they generated over $2M in pipeline from just two of the first events using this strategy.


[D2L went with a slightly different approach](https://www.navattic.com/blog/how-to-transform-customer-conferences-with-interactive-demos) at their user events, creating a “choose your own adventure” kind of experience.


Attendees could walk up to a demo station, select a specific interest area, and start going through a demo on an iPad.


This setup made for:


1. **A more personalized experience post-event.** Users could explore other areas of the product relevant to their interests.
2. **Better insights for the team.** Seeing which features drew the most interest was a good learning for future events (and GTM positioning in general).


*“We got a lot of positive feedback and we're definitely going to continue to develop and improve this experience for our future events,”* Sammi shares.


You could also try using interactive demos in[retargeting ads](https://www.navattic.com/blog/lead-funnel-product-led-content) on Google or LinkedIn, using compliant email addresses you collected or the conference attendee list. An interactive demo ad may be the push they need to learn more about your product and will keep it top of mind.


Don’t forget to keep a close eye on your Navattic’s analytics.


You’ll be able to see what parts of your product resonate most with prospects, giving you more ideas for what to feature in a webinar or conference talk and how to improve your demos over time.


**For more conference interactive demo ideas, check out:**


- [6 Tips to Prepare Perfect Conference Software Demos](https://www.navattic.com/blog/conference-software-demos)
- [Customer Show + Tell: Kristen Graves Hoppe: Demos at Conference Booths](https://www.navattic.com/blog/customer-show-and-tell-conference-booths-demos)


### Use case 4: Agent on the website


If you’ve got a particularly complex product, or if you have a wide swath of international customers, it can be tough to design a single product tour that works for everyone.


An[AI demo agent](https://www.navattic.com/blog/where-to-use-ai-demo-agents) can solve both problems.


Rather than following one set route, it can navigate to any part of your product, depending on what visitors say they’re interested in.


Plus, they’re always on, and they can respond in any language.


The[team at Bloomerang](https://www.navattic.com/customer/highlights/bloomerang) was looking for a way to help visitors who arrive at their site with very different questions about their full suite of products.


A Navattic Agent Demo seemed like a good solution, so they ran an A/B test, pitting the agent demo alongside their standard product tour for over 30 days.


The agent demo had a **113% lift in conversion rate** , generating roughly $16K more pipeline.


*“We noticed a clear difference in how prospects engaged with the agent,”* the team points out. *“More people are raising their hands after taking the agentic tour instead of the normal one.”*


Middle of funnel


Prospects at this stage are actively evaluating solutions.


As opposed to other MOFU content, interactive demos provide deeper insights into your product’s capabilities, helping potential customers see how it addresses their specific pain points.


### Use case 1: Self-serve sales demo automation


It’s impossible to know what every prospect is looking for in your product.


Even if you ask every prospect the same disco questions, you still may not get the answers you need (and you risk making them repeat the same answers they gave your competitor earlier that week).


Giving live demos isn’t the answer either. Designing and presenting them takes whole chunks out of an SE’s day.


According to our State of Demo Automation report, SEs run about 7 demos a week, and[94% run repetitive demos](https://www.navattic.com/report/state-of-demo-automation-2026) at least sometimes.


[Navattic Launchpad](https://www.navattic.com/blog/why-we-built-launchpad) can help your reps and SEs uncover what prospects care most about before you jump on a live call, while giving those high-intent leads a taste of your product.


[Jen Andretta’s team at Simfoni](https://www.navattic.com/blog/how-simfoni-transfored-their-demo-process) , for example, compiled a library of 30 interactive demos covering core platform features, with specialty product showcases against competitors.


They made these demos available through Launchpad, so their sales team could pick and choose which ones to send to potential customers – and personalize demos based on what AEs knew about their prospects.


Even the VP of sales got jazzed about how easy it was to get people’s attention: *“He sent a Navattic demo to a COO and got so excited that the prospect looked at it 5 times in 30 minutes,”* says Jen.


**Learn how Launchpad can help you build a more effective and efficient selling motion here:**[How SE Teams Are Using Navattic](https://www.navattic.com/blog/how-se-teams-are-using-navattic)


### Use case 2: SMB lead qualification with agents


Most AE and SE teams are strapped for time. Meeting with every lead that comes in is virtually impossible.


But those SMB leads could still be valuable – you never know what startup is going to become a unicorn in the next year or two.


Agentic demos help your team serve, and even convert, those smaller customers.


[Elizabeth Johnstone](https://www.linkedin.com/in/elizabeth-jp/) at Productboard uses Navattic agents to give those low-touch, self-serve prospects a real, interactive product experience 24/7.


She notes, *“It’s especially useful when they’re interested but not quite ready to hop on a call with a human.”*


For[Peyton Walbeck](https://www.linkedin.com/in/peyton-walbeck/) at Nectar, Navattic Agents are a way to protect the GTM team’s time.


*“Agents give prospects a simple, self-guided way to evaluate our product and determine fit, while freeing up the sales team to focus their time on strike zone opportunities.”*


### Use case 3: Email nurture campaigns


If you’ve already got someone’s email, chances are they are somewhat interested in your product.


Keep their attention by sending them useful and engaging emails. For example, instead of sending a static case study, send them an interactive walkthrough of a customer’s instance or particular feature.


If you’re nurturing free trialers, try inserting[mini-tutorial interactive demos](https://www.navattic.com/blog/interactive-demos-in-onboarding-email-drips) (each with just a few steps) in your emails that push them toward the action you want them to take next.


**To incorporate interactive demos in your outbound emails, read:**[Email Marketing Strategies for Product Demos](https://www.navattic.com/blog/email-marketing-strategies-product-demos)


### Use case 4: Sales outreach & SDR enablement


SDRs can use interactive demos in cold outreach and follow-up emails to stand out and promote engagement.


If your SDRs use Launchpad, they can pull the interactive demos they want to send straight from the[Chrome extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/navattic-launchpad/niekkpiejdapnjipjciadeddkpnpbbik) – and personalize them for prospects on the fly.


[Bloomreach’s](https://www.navattic.com/blog/how-bloomreach-scales-product-experiences) team built about 20 tours in Launchpad expressly for this purpose.


Allowing their sales team to share these demos with potential customers both qualifies bad leads out and educates the great ones, ensuring live demos are (1) worth solution consultants’ and reps’ time, and (2) go off smoothly.


Per Demo Engineering Manager, Vanessa Sedo:


*“We didn’t really have a quick, ‘Here, try now,’ type of trial. Interactive demos were a way for them to see the product. And truthfully, a way to get prospects to opt out. We wanted better qualified deals.”*


**For more on sales outreach, check out:**[How to Use Interactive Demos for Sales Leave Behinds](https://www.navattic.com/blog/interactive-demos-sales-leave-behinds)


### Use case 5: Buyer intent data


Once your SDRs and AEs are sending out interactive demos regularly, you’ll want to understand not just *who* viewed them but *how* those prospects engaged.


Pairing Navattic interactive demos with a digital sales room like[trumpet](https://www.sendtrumpet.com/) helps centralize content delivery and engagement analytics in one place.


From there, both use Navattic and digital sales rooms to track prospect interactions and send data directly to Slack or via email notifications.


Together, reps get a complete view of buyer intent, helping them prioritize accounts and tailor their next outreach.


As[Alex Harris from Coupa explains](https://www.navattic.com/blog/interactive-demos-digital-sales-rooms) ,


*“The power of combining Navattic interactive demos into our trumpet Pods is a game-changer for us, especially for organizations who may be very early into the buying journey but want to see our solution. Using both helps us truly understand how serious a prospect may be about entering a buying process with us.”*


With this data, teams can:


- Identify which prospects are most engaged and likely to convert
- See which demo content drives the most activity
- Personalize follow-ups with specific product features or use cases


If you’re planning on turning this intent into more of a structured ABM campaign,[Corinna Owens](https://www.navattic.com/blog/how-to-turn-interactive-demo-engagement-into-buying-signals) , Founder of Fractional ABM, suggests focusing specifically on four key metrics:


1. **Time spent per section** , so you know what they really care about.
2. **Demo completion** , so you know where to pick back up in a follow-up email or on a call.
3. **Drop-off** , so you know where people are losing interest, and can rework that demo.
4. **Repeat visits** , so you know someone is truly invested in your product.


*“When someone is willing to spend time with your product experience, when they’re clicking through a demo, choosing a path, spending time on a feature, coming back more than once, that matters,”* she says.


Tracking user behavior helps your sales team prioritize high-value accounts and determine the most strategic way to convert them.


**Hint:** Another fantastic source of intent data is your[agentic demo](https://www.navattic.com/blog/best-practices-for-sales-agentic-demos) transcript. You can see what questions a prospect asked, what objections they had, and tailor follow-up accordingly.


Bottom of funnel


B2B buyers expect a highly tailored buying experience, especially if they’ve already browsed your content, seen an ad or two, and chatted with a BDR.


Interactive demos provide hands-on engagement aligning with their specific needs.


### Use Case 1: Personalized sales demos


A case study about a company of a similar size in a similar industry is a good proof point.


An interactive demo that highlights the most relevant features to a prospect’s specific use case? A far more compelling proof point that gives prospects access to your product right away.


Navattic’s Launchpad Chrome Extension makes it easy to find, customize, and share interactive demos.


Instead of Slacking an SE to figure out which demo to send, reps can browse pre-call demos themselves, then drop them straight into prospect emails or LinkedIn DMs.


[Mathieu Govoni](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mathieu-govoni-533aab130/?originalSubdomain=uk) , an AE at Productboard, shares, *“What I appreciate most about Navattic is how easy it is to share interactive product demos. It’s a great way to let prospects experience value early in the sales cycle.”*


**Learn how to customize your demos to each buyer:**[How to Personalize Demos for ABM Campaigns](https://www.navattic.com/blog/how-to-personalize-product-demos-for-abm-campaigns)


### Use Case 2: Demos as a post-call follow up


Giving your fans a demo to show their colleagues increases your chances of winning over the naysayers faster.


[Sourceday](https://www.navattic.com/customer/highlights/sourceday) , a modern purchase order management platform, uses[demo automation](https://www.navattic.com/blog/demo-automation) built with Navattic to give product overviews to champions earlier in the sales funnel.


*“We are using these demos to enable champions to position the product internally without the need for multiple product demos throughout the sales cycle.”*


Navattic’s Launchpad makes this strategy more scalable, allowing your sales team to:


- Pull templated demos from a Chrome extension
- Customize them for each prospect.
- Embed them in emails and decks.


On the backend, reps can see where prospects spend the most time, a great place to start their next conversation.


*“With demo automation as part of our sales rep playbook, our SCs are spending 30% less time on early-stage demos and can focus on higher-value, more strategic deals,”* the team emphasizes.


### Use Case 3: High-level sandbox


Many buyers insist on getting their own sandbox. But sometimes those demo environments can come with a complex setup, and that doesn’t always leave a great first impression.


With[sandbox demos](https://docs.navattic.com/sandbox-demos) , you can make the process more seamless, using flashing[Beacons and Triggers](https://docs.navattic.com/flows#0KIKW) to show prospects exactly what to do and nudge them toward all the aha moments you want them to experience.


[Alexander Yant’s team at Slope](https://www.navattic.com/blog/customer-interview-series-personalized-demo-environments-with-alexander-yant) uses sandbox demos to give users confidence that their product does what they say it does, without making it seem complex.


*“Slope is a clinical trial execution platform for research sites, so they know when they need kits, where their kits are, where their samples are, and that everything is getting to where it should be and everyone is communicating.*


*We use Navattic to show that effectively, providing a tailored demo experience that communicates what we do clearly, especially since it’s pretty novel within the space.”*


To make the experience feel even more real, Alex personalizes each demo.


*“As soon as somebody comes to us, we can plug in their research site. So they see their name on the page, their title, and their site in the demo environment. It gives it a much more, not only personalized but warmer experience.”*


This helps them get the most out of their POC and reduces friction in the decision-making process.


### Use Case 4: Proof-of-Concept (POC) support


Spinning up a new proof of concept for every prospect who wants to try your product is a near-impossible task, especially for a small team.


You’d be surprised how close you can get to a POC with a[self-guided demo](https://www.navattic.com/blog/self-guided-demo) .


[Jakub Suchy at HAProxy](https://www.navattic.com/blog/customer-show-and-tell-demonstrating-technical-interfaces) , for example, has used Navattic plus a mix of AI tools and emulators to build interactive demos of Visual Studio Code, the Windows interface, Mac’s Finder, and other tough-to-replicate command-line interfaces.


*“I believe in creating demos that truly engage the audience and make them feel like they're experiencing the real product,”* Jakub explains.


*“My end goal is to use demos that convince customers and prospects that our product does what we say it does. And anything (really anything) can be recreated. There are ways to simulate any experience in a browser.”*


Read the[whole interview with Jakub](https://www.navattic.com/blog/customer-show-and-tell-demonstrating-technical-interfaces) to see exactly how he’s turned demos into POCs.


### Use Case 5: Post-sale and enablement


Because they’re so dynamic,[agentic demos](https://www.navattic.com/product/agent-demos) are a great way to kick off user onboarding.


New users can ask all kinds of questions to understand how your product works. And those questions get funneled straight to your CS team.


With that data at their fingertips, CSMs can:


- Better understand what’s going on in each account (who is a power user, who needs a bit more hand-holding, what problems they are experiencing)
- What other materials might be helpful to send customers to encourage adoption based on the kinds of questions they ask the agent
- How to make the most of upcoming live calls, by showing some complex features live


And remember, agents are good at selling, too.[Simfoni](https://www.navattic.com/blog/how-simfoni-transfored-their-demo-process) embedded agentic demos in their client portal to promote upsell and cross-sell opportunities.


*“They’re highlighted in yellow as specialty products. So if a customer wants to see something they don’t have today, they can just click it and say ‘View demo’ to see how it works.”*


On the backend, the CSM gets alerted and can step in with an AE to chat with the customer.


Agentic demos aren’t just for customers, though. They’re great for training internal folks, too.


When new reps join, they have to ramp up quickly, and agents are much more engaging teachers than call recordings.


[As one G2 user](https://www.g2.com/products/navattic/reviews/navattic-review-13870219?expanded=focused-review#focused-review) remarks, *“The AI bot’s capability to understand the context and respond accordingly is really good, which makes the overall experience feel more natural and useful.”*


Partner enablement is yet another prime use case for demos.[Intermedia](https://www.navattic.com/blog/how-to-scale-global-sales-enablement) , for instance, is using demos to train more than 7,500 channel partners across the globe.


They’ve embedded them directly into their LMS, and with one-click translation, they can educate partners regardless of what language they speak.


Bonus Use Case: G2 and other review sites


There’s one more use case we think has huge upside: review sites.


Review sites are one of the first places prospects visit in their vendor research. And while powerful messaging, screenshots, and positive customer feedback can help influence a buyer’s decision, your review site profiles may not highlight the full scope of what your product can do.


Even videos don’t do your product justice. Plus, they’re tough to maintain. Every time you update your product, it costs time and money to produce a new, accurate piece of content.


You can overcome those issues and get prospects’ hands on your product faster by adding Navattic demos to your G2 and TrustRadius profiles.


Inserting interactive demos in your product listings only takes a few steps.
